# Demo

```{r}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/scout.db")
postings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "scout_postings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
 
jobs = postings |>
  dplyr::select(company, title, location_state, remote, category, posted_at, last_seen_at) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::ends_with("_at"), as.Date),
                days_open = as.numeric(last_seen_at - posted_at))

jobs

jobs |>
  # I want to move UOA being a job postibg to category
  dplyr::group_by(category)|>
  dplyr::summarize(postings = dplyr::n(), remote_share = mean(remote))

# Among full-time postings, which states have the highest remote share? (Deviation from answers in the slides)

jobs |>
  dplyr::group_by(category, location_state) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    postings = dplyr::n(),
    remote_share = mean(remote)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(remote_share)) |>
  na.omit()

con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/midwest_airbnb.db")
listings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "listings") |>
  tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
dplyr::glimpse(listings)

listings |> dplyr(group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarise(count = dplyr::n()))

table(listings$city) # Returns a named vector for listings by city

# For entire homes (room_type == "Entire home/apt") that sleep four or more, what is the median price in each city?

listings |>
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt" & accommodates >= 4
  ) |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(median_price = median(price)) -> q2
q2

# Add price_per_person = price / accommodates. Which three listings are cheapest per person? Believe them?

listings |> 
  dplyr::mutate(price_per_person = price / accommodates) |> 
  # For the sake of printing neatly, I will reduce the number of cols
  dplyr::select(city,host_name, name, price, accommodates, price_per_person) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(price_per_person) |> 
  head(3)
  
# Which five host_names have the most listings?
# Host names aren't unique

listings |> dplyr::count(host_name, sort = T)

# This is better for finding unique hosts
listings |> dplyr::count(host_name, host_id, sort = T)

```
